verdict: Leads fell sharply this week; cost per lead is rising and needs attention.
narrative: In the last 28 days, Liferun received 125 leads at a cost of $16.61 per lead — but this week alone, leads dropped 49% against the prior seven days while cost per lead climbed 38%, a combination that signals the paid campaigns are working harder for fewer results. A confirmed gap in ad delivery, including at least one day with no spend at all, drove part of that shortfall; budget continuity is being stabilised now. Google Ads spent $485 this period with no attributed leads, and that channel is being reviewed to determine whether spend should be paused or redirected while tracking is corrected. On the pipeline side, no deals have been recorded as closed this period, and the follow-up process between incoming leads and activated appointments is being tightened. The focus over the next seven days is restoring consistent daily delivery on Meta, resolving Google attribution, and moving several overdue build items — including landing pages and creative — across the finish line.

highlights.phrase: leads received in the last 28 days, all from Meta
cost per lead this period, up 38% versus the prior seven days
spent on Google Ads this period with zero leads attributed

watch_item.issue: Ad delivery is breaking on at least 8 days this period, including a complete stop on September 17, causing lead volume to drop and cost per lead to spike.
watch_item.fix: Budget continuity and billing are being confirmed this week to eliminate zero-spend days and restore steady daily delivery.
